title: Track and field: Hamline Elite Meet is this week - NewsBreak
text:
By Mike Shaughnessy Sun ,
17 hours ago
South girls, Eagan boys finish first at Wildcat Invitational
One of the most anticipated events of the high school track and field season takes place this week when top athletes from across the state converge on Hamline University for the Hamline Elite Meet.
No team scores or enrollment divisions. Just the best against the best, based on results from the first few weeks of the 2026 season. Elite Meet field events begin at 5 p.m. Friday, April 24, with the first track event – the boys 100-meter preliminaries – starting at 5:15.
Except for the 100 dash, all events are finals-only, with nine athletes for the shorter races up to 12 for some field events and as many as 16 for distance events.
Athletes accepted into the meet won’t be announced until Thursday afternoon, but a number of from the South Suburban Conference are likely to be considered. Burnsville senior Carley LaMotte finished second in the girls 1,600 at last year’s Elite Meet and has the top reported time in the state (4 minutes, 55.33 seconds) this year.
Lakeville South’s Eva Welsch is defending Class 3A champion in the 100 hurdles. Lakeville North junior Kiah Blalark is a candidate to be chosen in the girls sprints, and LaMotte and Farmington junior Lauren Lansing have the No. 2 and 3 times in the state in the 800.
Rosemount senior Adam Hanson is first on the boys shot put honor roll with a top throw of 59-6.5. Farmington junior Aaron Geiken has the top reported times in the 110 and 300 hurdles.
Mega Meet
Lakeville North’s annual track and field invitational, the Mega Meet, will be 10 a.m. Saturday, April 25. The event is expected to attract more than a dozen schools in the boys and girls divisions, with Apple Valley, Burnsville and Trinity at River Ridge among those signed up.
Lakeville North is defending Mega Meet champion in the boys and girls divisions.
Wildcat Invitational
Lakeville South’s girls won their third meet of the season, taking first at the Eagan Wildcat Invitational on Tuesday and finishing more than 70 points ahead of runner-up Eagan.
Eagan was the winner of the boys meet, with Apple Valley and Burnsville taking second and third.
The Lakeville South girls had victories at the Wildcat Invitational from Faye Braun in the 800 (2:29.06), Chloe Thoennes in the 1,600 (5:31.87), Eva Welsch in the 100 hurdles (14.87) and 300 hurdles (45.12), the 4x200 relay (1:44.50), the 4x800 relay (9:57.20), Allie Rivers in the discus (113-11) and Teagan Bishop in the triple jump (35-0).
Ella Walters won the 400 in 1:00.08 for Eagan’s top individual finish.
Apple Valley was third in the girls team standings but had seven event winners – Kya Myers in the 100 (12.34) and 200 (25.69), Sophia Maier in the 3,200 (12:03.44), Mila Carnahan in the shot put (37-1.5), Avery Gibson in the high jump (5-1), and Leah Rudashevsky in the pole vault (11-7) and long jump (17-7.25).
The Burnsville girls’ top finish was second in the 400 by Danielle Dundon, who was about four-tenths of a second behind Eagan’s Walters.
Event winners who helped Eagan win the boys team championship included Ethan Wilske in the 800 (1:57.20), Liam Frank in the 1,600 (4:30.86), Evan Helgeson in the 300 hurdles (40.31), Harrison Brandt in the shot put (47-9.5)
Apple Valley’s boys finished second, about 24 points behind Eagan. Taking first place for the Eagles were Clifford Jones in the 100 (11.03), Abdishakur Mohamud in the 3,200 (10:29.30), Q Barnslater in the 110 hurdles (15.00), the 4x100 relay (42.83) and Avery Buckner in the long jump (21-10).
Caleb Kamara in the 200 (21.91), Keon Lloyd in the high jump (6-2) and Thomas Subah in the triple jump (45-6.25) were the Burnsville boys’ event winners at the Wildcat Invitational.
